questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Being able to experience a different culture, where I would be able to communicate with the locals in their own language. It was also really important to me, that the school was challenging and on a higher educational level.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were several information and orientation classes that is provided upon arrival. This is also a really good way to meet new people.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: several options in the form of dorm rooms. It was okay, but I found the dorms were in poor conditions, and very expensive.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: The dorms had kitchens, but all cutlery and poots and pans, were not provided.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Very nice to live close to the university, and it is the most amazing location. 30 min walks to city center, or faster if you take the bus (which is free if you're under 21, and have a young Scots card, which can be applied for). The dorms itself are in poor quality, but if you go for the more expensive options, they should be better. It took 10 minutes to walk to campus from my dorm in Finniestion.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Horrible course registration process. They will not let you choose the courses that you find the most interesting, and they prioritise the students enrolled in the latest semester. 

There is enough space for everyone, but you are not guaranteed a spot on specific courses, no matter how early you apply. 

Furthermore is the registration very late in the semester - which means you risk not having your courses when they actually start. This is not something to stress about though, as that is how they build up their semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You are provided assistance through an email. This was really helpfull and sorted all my problems. Definitely the way forward.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I only got one of the classes that i actually wanted, and had to settle for other classes. These other classes were relevant for my studies, but it was annoying.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress, but prepare yourself for a vary different and ineffective system compared to KU.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took lvl 4 courses which were on a high academic level, especially because it was in english and among native english speakers.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Quite similar, with few seminars, where you actually had to be there (I think this is specific for lvl 4 courses, lvl 1 and 2 had a lot of classes during the week). I only had class on tuesday and friday.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Family Law
Law and Genetics
Scottish Legal History Honors

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: International Family law were very interesting, and resembled a class you could take at home.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Loads of clubs and activities to join. The sports facilities were also really good.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: They had a hiking club that was cool.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Just travel all over Scotland and England. I also went to Ireland. They also have great football matches and rugby, which is cool.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Kinda easy. People were really nice and helpfull in general. Both people related to school and completely randoms. The Scots are a really nice people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't expect to make friends with a lot of local students, but they are nice, and always ready to help.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendlyness, and the drinking/partying culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't stress - Go to the student events (how you make friends in the beginning) - chose a dorm close to campus.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be friendly and open.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living on my own in a different country for a longer period of time.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Living on my own in a different country for a longer period of time.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
